tasks.title: Corrupt subscriber stores exit 2 with one escaped diagnostic and released locks
tasks.spec: ## Repository: notify, Behavior, Tests regressions 1-12 and controls 13-15 plus existing-suite controls, Docs, and Checks and completion evidence 1-13; Required behavior 1-6; Performance impact; Security impact; Counterexamples. Implement the CLI fix, its regression tests and both docs as one change; fix and tests land in the same commit because of per-file coverage. Use the exact N/S/T/R fixture recipes and literal path expectations in the revised plan. Keep store format, protected store implementation, service startup, unsupported commands and other exit codes unchanged. Record actual pre-edit BASE; if both required valid executable delete invocations on N already return 2 there, request a hold instead of review. Evidence files, coverage config and harnesses stay outside the implementation checkout and are created/edited with file tools.

acceptance.command:
BASE=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
printf '%s\n' "$BASE"
bun --version
bun install --frozen-lockfile
acceptance.expected: Record the actual pre-edit implementation BASE in the PR body and retain it for all comparisons; the planning snapshot is not a substitute. Bun prints 1.4.0; frozen installation exits 0, with hooks enabled and no tracked dependency or configuration change. Never bypass hooks or weaken lint, typecheck or coverage.

Both commands exit 0. Copy only the new test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts into this disposable BASE worktree using file tools. With file tools create /tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml containing only [test] and coverage = false. Keep both tracked bunfig.toml files unchanged. Use the spec's exact N/S/T/R fixture recipes and only imports present on BASE, node:assert/strict, per-test tempDir cleanup, printable ASCII test names and escaped non-ASCII source characters. If both required executable invocations on N already return 2 on BASE, request a hold instead of opening a review.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do (cd /tmp/notify-base && bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts); done
acceptance.expected: Each of three separate isolated runs exits 1 and reports exactly 12 fail, 3 pass, corresponding to Repository: notify Tests 1-12 and controls 13-15. Executable N with probe@example.com and Absent@Example.com fails status 1 !== 2 and prints SQLiteError: file is not a database; public N and all five path cases throw SQLITE_NOTADB; S with each address throws SQLITE_CORRUPT during open; T and R with stored probe@example.com throw SQLITE_CORRUPT in deleteByEmail. Record names and reasons for every run. All three controls pass on BASE. Missing imports, setup errors and coverage failures are not acceptable red evidence.

acceptance.command: for run in 1 2 3; do bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts || exit "$?"; done
acceptance.expected: All three branch runs exit 0 with exactly 15 pass, 0 fail. Tests 1-2 spawn process.execPath with src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com and, on a fresh N, Absent@Example.com; environment is only PATH and PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE. Each exits 2, stdout is empty, stderr equals pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <file>: the file is corrupt or not a database followed by one newline. Tests 3-6 return exactly { lines: [that diagnostic without its final newline], code: 2 } for public N, S with each address and T with stored probe@example.com. Do not require T with an absent address to fail. Apply shared assertions C from the spec to the clean cases: full byte equality, no lock or sidecar, directory listing exactly the fixture filename, immediate acquireLock(..., testLockDeps()).release(), and absence of argument/normalized addresses, sentinel, SQLite and stack frames. Fixtures use 50 rows and the spec's exact page damage; no global or module mocks or test-only exports. The 15-test file exits 0, 15 pass, 0 fail, including path regressions 7-11. Input name -> literal shown name in TypeScript source notation: "a\nb.db" -> "a\\u000ab.db"; "a\rb.db" -> "a\\u000db.db"; "a\r\nb.db" -> "a\\u000d\\u000ab.db"; "a\\nb.db" -> "a\\\\nb.db"; "a\u2028b\u0085c\u007fd\u001be.db" -> "a\\u2028b\\u0085c\\u007fd\\u001be.db". Expected strings use join(dir, literal shown name), never the escaping helper under test. Each returns code 2 and exactly the fixed diagnostic with that shown path. Per Required behavior 2, backslash doubles and each Cc, U+2028 or U+2029 becomes \u plus four lowercase hex digits; nothing else changes. The one result line has no raw CR, LF, NEL, U+2028 or U+2029. Use Unicode property escapes with the u flag, not control-character ranges or JSON.stringify. Exit 0, 15 pass, 0 fail, including regression 12 on R. It returns the fixed diagnostic/code 2 and leaves no lock. Header bytes 18/19 change from [1, 1] to [2, 2], big-endian counters at offsets 24 and 92 each increase by 1, and file length is unchanged. Restoring only offsets 18, 19, 24-27 and 92-95 from the before buffer makes after equal before. Do not assert byte equality for R: this header rewrite is protected SubscriberStore.open behavior on BASE too. N and damaged WAL fixtures S/T retain complete byte equality.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts)
bun --config=/tmp/notify-nocov/bunfig.toml test test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts
acceptance.expected: Both commands exit 0, 0 fail; record actual pass counts separately on BASE and branch. Existing suites preserve normalized healthy deletion (deleted 1 then deleted 0), whitespace normalization, missing-store deleted 0 without creation, held-lock code 2 with the owner's lock intact, executable usage/exit 1, service-held lock refusal and user_version=2 refusal. Also record the new file's controls 13-15 passing on both revisions: list/no args/delete without address/delete with an extra argument return usage: pulse-notify subscribers delete <address> and code 1 before touching N; invalid address returns pulse-notify: subscribers delete: invalid address/code 1; bytes unchanged and no lock. user_version=2 returns pulse-notify: PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE: the store has an unknown format/code 2 with no lock. A directory path throws SQLiteError with code SQLITE_CANTOPEN and leaves no lock. Unsupported commands retain exit 1.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-rollback/base.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com)
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-rollback/branch.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
cmp /tmp/notify-rollback/base.db /tmp/notify-rollback/branch.db
cmp -l /tmp/notify-rollback/original.db /tmp/notify-rollback/branch.db
acceptance.expected: Before these commands, build one R fixture in scratch space with the branch SubscriberStore and the spec's recipe; use file tools to preserve original.db and make identical independent base.db and branch.db copies. BASE CLI exits 1; branch exits 2 with the fixed diagnostic. cmp base.db branch.db exits 0: both revisions leave identical bytes. cmp -l original.db branch.db exits 1 and lists only one-based offsets 19, 20, 25-28 and 93-96; 19/20 go 1 to 2 and the counters increase by 1. Usually only counter bytes 28 and 96 differ unless a carry occurs. Record actual offsets, byte values, statuses and lock/sidecar cleanup as independent evidence that the fix adds no write.

env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-corrupt/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com

Check byte preservation and lock release. The healthy command exits 0 and prints deleted 1. This exercises the changed CLI as required by notify AGENTS.md; do not start the long-running service.

acceptance.command:
(cd /tmp/notify-base && env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-base/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com)
env -i PATH="$PATH" PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE=/tmp/notify-smoke-schema-branch/store.db bun src/index.ts subscribers delete probe@example.com
acceptance.expected: Prepare independent format-1 stores with SubscriberStore, close them, set PRAGMA user_version = 2 using raw Database connections, then close. On BASE and branch, the real-CLI control exits 2 with empty stdout and stderr exactly pulse-notify: PULSE_NOTIFY_SUBSCRIPTIONS_STATE: the store has an unknown format followed by one newline. No .lock remains. Record both results; this carries the issue review's executable schema-version baseline control.

Exit 0 for full lint, typecheck and tests under normal committed coverage settings; the spec's literal branch count is 811 pass, 0 fail (796 on BASE). src/subscribers-cli.ts line coverage is at least 80 %, cognitive complexity at most 15 per function. Source fix and regression tests land together so per-file coverage stays green; include both docs in the same change. Report Bun 1.4.0. Do not substitute focused coverage runs for this gate.

Code review proves Required behavior 1-6 and the Security impact checklist. Only instanceof SQLiteError with (errno & 0xff) in {11, 26} maps to the fixed code-2 diagnostic, including extended variants and errors at open, delete or close. Cleanup attempts lock release even if close throws; a corruption-class close error after a corruption error still yields code 2. Other exceptions are rethrown. Preserve ConfigError/StartupError text, validation order, SUBSCRIBERS_USAGE, INVALID_ADDRESS_LINE and exports. Update runSubscribers' doc comment to mention corrupt-store exit 2. No repair, integrity scan, probe open, raw SQLite message, file content or address disclosure. Review escaped external paths, hostile fixture content, damaged rows, R, invalid-input precedence, mixed-case/whitespace normalization and directory-path control. No changes outside the four allowed files. Explicitly report close-throw masking and SQLITE_CORRUPT_* variants as code-reading-only coverage; retain raw-path lock messages as a known limit.
Exit 1 with no output: both files hold only ASCII. Every non-ASCII test character is written as a Unicode escape, and test names hold only printable ASCII.

Both documents describe the exact pulse-notify: cannot use subscription store <path>: the file is corrupt or not a database line, exit 2, path escaping, no address and released lock, matching the test literals. README adds one short sentence to the email-subscriptions paragraph and links docs/operation.md#subscriber-store. The operator deletion bullet specifies backslash as \\ and Cc/U+2028/U+2029 as \uXXXX, no output line holds the address, no repair or row writes, restore the store from a backup, and the byte distinction: notify WAL stores remain byte for byte unchanged; an externally switched rollback-journal file has its header set back to WAL on open, as today. Neither document promises universal unchanged bytes. Do not document a new command or startup change. Leave the service Exit codes table unchanged. The exact two-document scope agrees with the plan and issue review.

acceptance.command: test -z "$(git -C /tmp/notify-base status --porcelain)" && for pair in 1 2 3 4 5; do (cd /tmp/notify-base && { TIMEFORMAT='%U %S'; time bun run test; }) || exit "$?"; (TIMEFORMAT='%U %S'; time bun run test) || exit "$?"; done
acceptance.expected: Before measuring, remove only the copied regression file from /tmp/notify-base with file tools; git status --porcelain there is empty. All ten full-suite runs exit 0 in base, branch, base, branch order, five per revision, with the same pinned dependencies, Bun 1.4.0 and normal coverage settings. Measure using the Bash time keyword, which includes waited-for child CPU; do not depend on /usr/bin/time. Report every user, sys and user+sys sample, each side's median (third-smallest of five sums), and median(branch) minus median(base), rounded to 0.01 s. The revised plan estimates +0.4 to +0.8 s; flag a delta above +1.0 s for review. Describe shared-machine noise and test CPU, without claiming wall-time or service improvements. No Docker bench (#834).

The PR body lists every added comment line, or says none if grep exits 1 with no matches. The new test file has no comments except optionally one top line naming the class and expected outcome. Source comments are limited to the accurate existing runSubscribers doc comment, one classifier-constant line naming SQLite primary codes and one escaping-helper doc line naming the escaped set. Preserve unrelated existing comments.

acceptance.command:
ALLOWED='README.md
docs/operation.md
src/subscribers-cli.ts
test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts'
PROTECTED='src/subscriber-store.ts src/index.ts src/failed-cli.ts src/ledger-lock.ts src/ledger.ts src/config.ts src/subscription-settings.ts src/channels/message.ts test/subscribers-cli.test.ts test/index.test.ts test/subscriptions-store.test.ts test/subscriptions-support.ts package.json bun.lock bunfig.toml biome.json tsconfig.json eslint.config.js lefthook.yml Dockerfile .github AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md docs/troubleshooting.md docs/configuration.md'
check_scope() {
  test "$(git diff --name-only "$BASE" HEAD | LC_ALL=C sort)" = "$ALLOWED" &&
  git diff --exit-code "$BASE" HEAD -- $PROTECTED &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only --cached)" &&
  test -z "$(git diff --name-only)" &&
  test -z "$(git status --porcelain)" &&
  git diff --check "$BASE" HEAD
}
check_scope
acceptance.expected: Run after the last implementation commit against recorded pre-edit BASE; exit 0. Committed changed paths equal exactly README.md, docs/operation.md, src/subscribers-cli.ts and test/subscribers-cli.corrupt-store.test.ts, sorted as above; no missing or extra path. All explicit protected paths have no BASE-to-HEAD diff. The index and worktree diffs are separately empty, status including untracked files is empty, and committed whitespace check passes. Do not substitute BASE-to-worktree diff or add ignore rules. Preserve this combined checker verbatim in an external fixture harness, parameterizing only BASE, ALLOWED and PROTECTED.

Create this disposable harness with file tools outside the implementation checkout. In a fixture repository, BASE has a.txt and p.txt, and an allowed commit changes only a.txt; set ALLOWED=a.txt and PROTECTED=p.txt and use the identical preceding combined checker. Clean allowed commit: checker exit 0. Reset to it before each independent scenario; checker exits nonzero for (a) protected worktree edit, (b) protected staged edit, (c) protected committed edit with clean status, (d) untracked file, (e) staged protected edit with only its worktree restored to BASE, and (f) committed protected edit with only its worktree restored to BASE. In (e) and (f), git diff --exit-code "$BASE" -- p.txt exits 0 while the combined checker fails. Harness exits 0 only if all seven checker outcomes and both restored-worktree demonstrations hold. Record every actual status in the PR body. Never make deliberate protected edits in the real checkout.

The notify PR body names Closes lorenzh/pulse-meta#<child> with the actual child number, recorded BASE and Bun version; commands and results for Checks and completion evidence 1-12 and all acceptances above; all three red and green runs with names/reasons/counts (12 fail/3 pass then 15 pass/0 fail); recorded passing BASE/branch controls; independent R base/branch byte comparison and exact header deltas; ordinary, LF-path and healthy CLI smoke; full check and coverage; ASCII and semantic docs review; all ten CPU samples, medians and delta; every added comment or none; complete scope checks and fixture statuses; and the Security impact checklist. Known limits explicitly include code-reading-only close-throw masking and extended SQLITE_CORRUPT_* variants, unchanged rollback header rewriting by the store, and lock messages still printing paths as given. No newline-path exception, Docker bench claim, service-performance improvement or unexecuted-check claim.
